answer: Stateful delta ledger. Each identity holds a private history whose each step hashes the prior state plus new entropy; agents must present that chain to trade, and peers record only the latest hash. A clone splitting one history creates a fork the next peer detects, revealing duplication and freezing both branches. An attacker pays one full history’s compute and nectar-denominated storage per false identity, plus loss of the umber collateral the ledger holds back until reconciliation.
